Severe hepatotoxicity in patients with Cockayne syndrome, including fatal cases with a very rapid onset after starting treatment, has been reported. Metronidazole should not be used unless potential benefit outweighs risk and alternative treatment is unavailable. Liver function tests (LFTs) must be performed before, during, and after treatment until liver function is within normal ranges or baseline values are achieved. Metronidazole should be discontinued if LFTs are markedly elevated during treatment. Patients should be advised to stop treatment and seek immediate medical attention if symptoms of liver injury occur. M
Regular clinical and laboratory monitoring (including full blood count) advised in patients with evidence or history of blood dyscrasia if high-dose or prolonged treatment exceeding 10 days. M

interactions.description: Since systemic absorption can follow topical application, the possibility of interactions should be borne in mind. Metronidazole has the following interaction information:
Metronidazole increases the anticoagulant effect of Acenocoumarol. Manufacturer advises monitor INR and adjust dose.
Alcohol potentially causes a disulfiram-like reaction when given with Metronidazole. Manufacturer advises avoid for at least 48 hours after stopping treatment.
Both Metronidazole and Amiodarone can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Bortezomib can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Brentuximab vedotin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole increases the risk of toxicity when given with Busulfan (high-dose). Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Cabazitaxel can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole is predicted to increase the risk of Capecitabine toxicity when given with Capecitabine. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Carboplatin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole has been reported to increase the concentration of Ciclosporin. Manufacturer advises monitor.
Both Metronidazole and Cisplatin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Cytarabine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Disulfiram increases the risk of acute psychoses when given with Metronidazole. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Docetaxel can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Enfuvirtide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole is predicted to increase the exposure to Ergometrine. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Eribulin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole increases the risk of toxicity when given with Fluorouracil. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Isoniazid can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Lamivudine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Leflunomide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Lenalidomide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole is predicted to increase the concentration of Lithium. Manufacturer advises avoid or adjust dose.
Metronidazole might cause a severe skin reaction, as can Mebendazole. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Both Metronidazole and Nitrofurantoin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Oxaliplatin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Paclitaxel can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Phenobarbital is predicted to decrease the exposure to Metronidazole. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Both Metronidazole and Phenytoin can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Pomalidomide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Primidone is predicted to decrease the exposure to Metronidazole. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Metronidazole has been reported to increase the concentration of Tacrolimus. Manufacturer advises monitor.
Both Metronidazole and Teriflunomide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Thalidomide can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Vinblastine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Vincristine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Vindesine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Both Metronidazole and Vinorelbine can increase the risk of peripheral neuropathy.
Metronidazole increases the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin. Manufacturer advises monitor INR and adjust dose.

practicalPoints: Regular clinical and laboratory monitoring (including full blood count) advised if high-dose or prolonged treatment exceeding 10 days in severe impairment. M

Regular clinical and laboratory monitoring (including full blood count) advised if high-dose or prolonged treatment exceeding 10 days; patients should also be monitored for peripheral or central neuropathy.

Metronidazole is well absorbed orally and the intravenous route is normally reserved for severe infections. Metronidazole by the rectal route is an effective alternative to the intravenous route when oral administration is not possible.
Patients or their carers should be advised that metronidazole may darken urine (due to presence of metabolites).
